title: Finite-sample likelihood-ratio operating characteristics for the SDCB near-pole-swap challenge

provenance.covariance_fixture_contract: OU process followed by a first-order low-pass instrument response; complete sampled covariance law

acquisition.sample_cost: one synthetic acquisition unit per time sample

lrt.rejection_rule: reject World B when ell(y)>tau_alpha; use randomized rejection on an atom at tau_alpha to attain the declared size
lrt.equal_prior_rule: choose World A when ell(y)>0, choose World B when ell(y)<0, and split ties 50/50

quadratic_form_reduction.distribution: central indefinite Gaussian quadratic form with eigenvalues of the symmetric G matrix

numerical_method.method: Imhof characteristic-function inversion for a weighted sum of independent chi-square(1) variables
numerical_method.independent_numerical_cross_check: separately evaluated quadrature implementations (SciPy quad and mpmath quadrature) on the same characteristic-function representation
numerical_method.integration_precision: mpmath 30 decimal digits for the independent quadrature check
numerical_method.status: preliminary numerical agreement; not a certified quadrature enclosure
numerical_method.future_methods: compare with Davies or another independently structured quadratic-form distribution implementation before qualification

fixed_sample_count_interval_sweep.interpretation: Among these six candidates only, interval 0.5 gives the greatest estimated LRT power and KL at fixed n=32. This is not a continuous or global design optimum; sample cost, elapsed time, and energy are distinct objectives.

exploratory_monte_carlo_check.interpretation: Exploratory consistency check only. The seed/PRNG manifest is not included in this fixture; do not treat this row as a reproducible qualification result.

negative_and_positive_controls.expected: Identical joint distributions; randomized size-alpha LRT has power alpha and equal-prior accuracy 0.5; deterministic tie conventions must not create a classifier advantage.
Distinct covariance kernels but weak finite-design discrimination; reproduce the frozen likelihood-ratio operating characteristics.
Applying the same permutation to both covariance matrices leaves every LRT operating characteristic unchanged.
The optimal equal-prior discrimination cannot worsen when the larger observation vector contains the smaller vector as a prefix.
Increasing independent additive readout noise cannot improve optimal discrimination for this observation channel.
Non-SPD/singular support, unknown covariance, nonfinite values, or numerical nonconvergence return explicit unsupported/error status; no jitter or silent covariance repair.

scope_exclusions: physical calibration, traceability, QUANT data, or field performance
claim_boundary: Preliminary numerical reference for a fixed, known, zero-mean, positive-definite Gaussian covariance pair under a frozen finite sampling design. It is not a Rust implementation pass, statistical qualification, physical validation, or superiority result.
